advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an alarm (or an unmatched-reason guard) covering interrupt reasons that match neither `bound-exceeded` nor `signal-unavailable`, so a future/typo reason still pages.
evidence: monitoring_autodeploy.tf:100 'review_interrupts ... rolled-up total, published but NOT alarmed'
observability.sh:215 'any future third reason is still counted somewhere; only the per-reason metrics are alarmed'
Only two alarm resources exist (monitoring_autodeploy.tf:113 review_interrupts_bound_exceeded, :152 review_interrupts_signal_unavailable); the prior single alarm on review_interrupts was removed
A new reason would match the rolled-up token grep (observability.sh:241) but neither reason-scoped ERE (observability.sh:248/252), so its per-reason metric stays 0 and never breaches
advisory.finding: A future/unknown interrupt reason will be counted in the rolled-up `review_interrupts` but is no longer alarmed by anything, so it pages nobody. Before this change the single alarm on `review_interrupts` fired on ANY reason; now only `bound-exceeded` and `signal-unavailable` have alarms and the rolled-up metric is explicitly de-alarmed, opening a silent-coverage gap for any new reason autodeploy.sh's marker() might emit.
scenarios: autodeploy.sh gains a third interrupt reason (e.g. a new fail-open path) and the marker's reason field is a value neither regex matches
A typo/rename in the reason string emitted by autodeploy.sh silently drops the interrupt out of both alarmed metrics
advisory.suggested_fix: Either keep a low-priority alarm on the rolled-up `review_interrupts` (or on a computed `review_interrupts - bound - signal` residual), or add a test asserting an unknown reason is surfaced, so a new/renamed reason cannot go silently unpaged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider reading the journal once and deriving all three interrupt counts from a single scan rather than three journalctl invocations.
evidence: Three consecutive calls: observability.sh:241 (review_interrupts), :247 (bound), :251 (signal) each invoke the helper -> three full journalctl scans
advisory.finding: The interrupt token is now scanned over the full unit journal three separate times per probe tick (rolled-up + two reason-scoped), each a fresh `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy.service | grep`, tripling the journal-read work for this marker on every timer fire.
scenarios: A large/long-lived rebar-autodeploy journal makes each probe tick read the whole journal three times

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add Terraform `moved` blocks (or accept a documented replace) for the `review_interrupts` alarm rename to the two per-reason alarms so `terraform apply` does not destroy coverage.
evidence: `search_files` for `moved` in infra/terraform returned only an unrelated comment at monitoring.tf:175 — no `moved` block exists to preserve state
File comment stresses this alarm is the ONLY signal: monitoring_autodeploy.tf:76 'that outage was INVISIBLE to every other alarm'
signal-unavailable block: monitoring_autodeploy.tf:173-182 with identical cadence and actions
Comment acknowledges intent to keep them identical: monitoring_autodeploy.tf:108 'Both alarms keep the pre-split 900s / 1-datapoint / Sum > 0 / notBreaching cadence'
advisory.finding: The CloudWatch alarm resource is renamed from `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.review_interrupts` (alarm_name `rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts`) to two new resources with new addresses and new alarm_names, but no Terraform `moved` block or state migration is provided. `terraform apply` will therefore DESTROY the existing alarm and CREATE two new ones, leaving the 34cd failure mode unmonitored during the destroy→create window.
merged_from: The two new alarm resources are near-identical copies (same namespace, statistic, period=900, evaluation_periods=1, datapoints_to_alarm=1, threshold=0, comparison_operator, treat_missing_data, actions, tags) differing only in name/metric_name/description. This duplicated block invites configuration drift where a future cadence/action change is applied to one alarm but not the other.
scenarios: Operator runs `terraform apply`; the old alarm is deleted before/while the two replacements settle, and a review-interrupt during that gap pages nothing.
A dashboard or SNS runbook keyed on alarm_name `rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts` stops resolving after the rename.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `moved { from = aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.review_interrupts, to = aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.review_interrupts_bound_exceeded }` (and/or explicitly acknowledge the create-before-destroy) so the state transition preserves alarm coverage; audit dashboards/runbooks referencing the old alarm_name.
